title: Natural selection acts slowly, intermittently and on few species at a time

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Natural selection acts slowly, intermittently and on few species at a time

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Natural selection always acts very slowly, often only at long intervals of time, and generally on only a very few of the inhabitants of a region at the same time.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: On the other hand, I do believe that natural selection will always act very slowly, often only at long intervals of time, and generally on only a very few of the inhabitants of the same region at the same time.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter IV, “Natural Selection”; section “Slow action”. Scope: all organisms within a region over geological time

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch04-17: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.54

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Modern time series can test restricted temporal and regional versions. No existing resource observes selection consistently across all inhabitants and geological timescales.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate temporal rates of adaptive phenotypic or allele-frequency change and the fraction of co-occurring species showing selection in repeated community time series. Predominantly slow, episodic change affecting few species supports the claim; widespread rapid concurrent adaptation refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Very slowly' and 'long intervals' need arbitrary temporal thresholds.

Ecological abundance change is not equivalent to natural selection.

fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.61
discriminating power: 0.43
data adequacy: 0.43
analysis feasibility: 0.54
data existence: 0.66

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Geological rates are estimable from the fossil record, and generation-scale experiments show that selection need not be slow on an ecological clock. Which clock the wording uses is ambiguous, so the same data can be read as compatible or as a counterexample. Selection gradients for whole regional biotas are not in one open dataset, which limits the test to proxies and well-studied cases.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure rates of phenotypic and genomic change per generation and per geological interval, and the fraction of co-occurring species showing concurrent directional change. The claim would be confirmed if change is almost always geologically slow, intermittent, and limited to a small minority of species in a region; rapid, simultaneous responses in many co-occurring species would refute the strong reading. The word slowly still needs a declared timescale.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Field estimates of selection differentials are scattered across studies.

Slowly can mean per-generation selection or the geological appearance of new forms, and those are different tests.

Abundance change in monitoring series is not the same variable as selection.
